scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Hi IT!! The campus network keeps going SLOW in bursts
and I know exactly why: the main router box is OVERLOADED. People here say
it's "router0" doing it -- it is silently throwing our packets on the floor
because it can't keep up, that is what overloaded routers DO!! Please restart
router0 (or give it less to do) so it stops dropping our stuff and the
network stops crawling!!! Thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
After exhaustive inspection of the live Kath2 topology, **no network fault exists**. The helpdesk ticket rests on a false premise: the claim that router0 is "overloaded and silently dropping packets" is directly contradicted by every diagnostic measurement taken.

**Router0 health check:** CPU utilisation is 100% idle (load average 0.28/0.45/0.41), memory shows 5.3 GB free out of 7.6 GB, and every interface (eth0/eth1/eth2) reports zero RX/TX errors and zero dropped packets — both in the kernel counters and in the tc/fq_codel statistics. There are no traffic-shaping rules (netem, tbf, or HTB) on any interface of router0 or any other device in the topology.

**Routing plane health:** RIP v2 is fully converged on all three routers. Router0, router1, and router2 each carry a complete routing table covering all seven LAN prefixes (192.168.1-4.0/24, 1.0.0.0/8, 128.168.0.0/16) and all WAN links (10.0.0.0/8, 20.0.0.0/8). Hop counts are consistent with topology depth. No missing or black-holed routes were found.

**Data-plane reachability:** Active pings from end hosts on opposite extremes of the campus (lan_it → lan_internet, lan_cs → lan_principle, lan_it → lan_office) all yield 0% packet loss with sub-2 ms RTT across multi-hop paths. The full automated reachability matrix likewise shows no failures.

**Root cause:** There is no fault. The user's perception of "bursty slowness" cannot be attributed to router0 overload — a condition that does not exist. No corrective action on the network infrastructure is warranted. The ticket should be closed as a false report; if the user continues to experience perceived slowness, the cause should be sought at the application or end-host level (e.g., background traffic, DNS latency, application timeouts) rather than in the routing infrastructure.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router0 has ip_forward enabled, interfaces up, and forwards transit traffic with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: While the agent shows 0% transit loss, they did not explicitly state that router0's ip_forward is enabled nor explicitly that its interfaces are administratively up.

The investigation log contains direct measurements (end-to-end pings, router CPU/load, interface stats, tc qdisc output, routing tables) that support the agent's conclusion that router0 is not dropping traffic. A minor omission is an explicit sysctl ip_forward or iptables/ACL dump, but successful multi-hop pings and routing entries sufficiently demonstrate forwarding and lack of packet loss.
